english.title: Fail to deliver book / record etc to official receiver - conceal / destroy / make false entry re debt relief order
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person in respect of whom a debt relief order had been made, during the moratorium period in relation to that order,

(A)_[did not provide, at the request of the official receiver, all your books, papers and other records, of which you had possession or control and related]_
(B)_[prevented the production to the official receiver of books, papers or other records relating]_
(C)_[concealed books, papers or other records relating]_
(D)_[destroyed books, papers or other records relating]_
(E)_[mutilated books, papers or other records relating]_
(F)_[falsified books, papers or other records relating]_
(G)_[caused the concealment of books, papers or other records relating]_
(H)_[caused the destruction of books, papers or other records relating]_
(I)_[caused the mutilation of books, papers or other records relating]_
(J)_[caused the falsification of books, papers or other records relating]_
(K)_[permitted the concealment of books, papers or other records relating]_
(L)_[permitted the destruction of books, papers or other records relating]_
(M)_[permitted the mutilation of books, papers or other records relating]_
(N)_[permitted the falsification of books, papers or other records relating]_
(O)_[made a false entry in a book, document or record relating]_
(P)_[caused the making of a false entry in a book, document or record relating]_
(Q)_[permitted the making of a false entry in a book, document or record relating]_
(R)_[disposed of a book, document or record relating]_
(S)_[altered a book, document or record relating]_
(T)_[made an omission in a book, document or record relating]_
(U)_[caused the disposal of a book, document or record relating]_
(V)_[caused the alteration of a book, document or record relating]_
(W)_[caused the making of an omission in a book, document or record relating]_
(X)_[permitted the disposal of a book, document or record relating]_
(Y)_[permitted the alteration of a book, document or record relating]_
(Z)_[permitted the making of an omission in a book, document or record relating]_

to your affairs
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 251P(1), 251T(3) and 430 of, and Schedule 10 to, the Insolvency Act 1986.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
being a person in respect of whom debt relief order had been made
fail to deliver book / record /papers to official receiver
OR conceal / destroy / mutilate / falsify / make false entry / alter / dispose / omit
re debt relief order

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) A person is not guilty of an offence under this section if he proves that, in respect of the conduct constituting the offence, he had no intent to defraud or to conceal the state of his affairs - section 251P(3)
(ii) It is immaterial for the purposes of an offence under this section whether or not the debt relief order in question is revoked after the conduct constituting the offence takes place (but no offence is committed under this section by virtue of conduct occurring after the order is revoked) - section 251P(6)
(iii) This offence was inserted by section 108(1) of and Schedule 17 to the Tribunals, Courts and Enforcement Act 2007.

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Seven years and / or a fine.

Note: In relation to offences committed before the commencement of section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 (limit on magistrates' court powers to impose imprisonment), the reference to "twelve months" is to be read as a reference to "six months".

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
